items.title: Fibre dimension is preserved under the substitution a to a^n + b for large n
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms)

items.difficulty_reason: For a finite type ring map R -> S and elements a, b, if the fibres of f_a : Spec(S) -> A^1_R have dimension at most d, then for all large n the fibres of f_{a^n+b} have dimension at most d. The proof is a long sequence of reductions that each remove a hypothesis: from arbitrary R -> S to finite presentation by writing S as a quotient and using that the ideal is a union of finitely generated ideals, then to R of finite type over Z by a filtered colimit argument with a dimension bound descending along the colimit, and finally an induction on dim(R) that peels off a component of the complement of a distinguished open and applies the inductive hypothesis to R/I -> S/IS. The final assembly takes the maximum of the two thresholds. What makes this non-routine is that the dimension condition must be transported through each of these reductions in the correct direction, and the induction needs the complement to be cut out by an ideal so that dim(R/I) < dim(R). Retained author proof at lines 8612-8777.
